Strongest human evidence: Small sleep and sleep-restriction crossover trials
Studied doses and populations: 3 g before bedtime; adults with unsatisfactory sleep or experimentally restricted sleep
Supported findings: Possible short-term improvement in subjective sleep, fatigue and vigilance
Null or negative findings: Trials are tiny; no durable clinical or longevity outcomes
Certainty: Low for sleep; insufficient for longevity

Strongest human evidence: One four-week bisglycinate RCT plus broader magnesium-salt reviews
Studied doses and populations: 250 mg/day elemental magnesium in the bisglycinate trial; heterogeneous salts elsewhere
Null or negative findings: Meta-analysis found low/very-low-certainty evidence; sleep-duration improvement was nonsignificant
Certainty: Low for sleep; no form-specific longevity evidence

Strongest human evidence: Extensive exercise evidence; mixed cognitive RCTs and syntheses
Studied doses and populations: Common chronic research doses around 3–5 g/day; acute sleep-deprivation studies 0.2–0.35 g/kg
Supported findings: Established ergogenic role; possible small memory effects or protection under energetic stress
Null or negative findings: Largest preregistered cognition RCT found no significant primary effects; global cognition meta-analysis result was nonsignificant
Certainty: High for repeated high-intensity performance; Low–Moderate for cognition

Strongest human evidence: Small BP RCTs and seven-study meta-analysis
Supported findings: Approximately 3 mmHg pooled BP reduction; 1.6 g/day RCT was positive in prehypertension
Null or negative findings: No large outcomes trials; animal longevity findings do not demonstrate human lifespan extension
Certainty: Low–Moderate for BP; insufficient for longevity

Strongest human evidence: Nutrient-essentiality evidence and small maternal feeding trials
Studied doses and populations: 480 versus 930 mg/day total maternal choline; pregnancy-specific
Supported findings: Higher prenatal intake may affect infant processing and later sustained attention
Null or negative findings: Does not establish adult cognitive enhancement; choline, citicoline and alpha-GPC cannot be treated as interchangeable
Certainty: Moderate for nutritional adequacy; Low for prenatal cognitive effects; insufficient for adult enhancement

Strongest human evidence: Homocysteine RCT and adjunctive depression trials
Studied doses and populations: 113 micrograms/day nutritional study; 7.5–15 mg/day adjunctive psychiatric trials
Supported findings: Lowers homocysteine; 15 mg/day showed benefit in one small SSRI-resistant MDD trial
Null or negative findings: Lower-dose depression trial was negative; biomarker lowering is not proof of cardiovascular or longevity benefit
Certainty: Moderate for homocysteine; Low for adjunctive MDD; insufficient for longevity

Strongest human evidence: Established treatment of deficiency; RCTs and cognitive meta-analysis
Studied doses and populations: 1 mg/day in asymptomatic moderately deficient older adults
Supported findings: Corrects biochemical deficiency and prevents/treats recognized deficiency consequences
Null or negative findings: Correcting moderate asymptomatic deficiency did not improve neurologic or cognitive outcomes; no general cognitive benefit in nondeficient populations
Certainty: High for deficiency treatment; Moderate–High for no cognitive enhancement in replete/asymptomatic populations

Strongest human evidence: Large VITAL outcomes trial and fracture analysis
Studied doses and populations: 2,000 IU/day; 25,871 generally healthy midlife and older adults
Supported findings: Corrects deficiency; recognized bone, muscle and calcium-homeostasis roles
Null or negative findings: No reduction in primary cancer/CVD outcomes or total, nonvertebral or hip fractures in generally healthy adults not selected for deficiency
Certainty: High for deficiency-related indications; High for lack of broad primary-prevention benefit at this regimen

Supported findings: Improves vitamin K status; modest effects on selected bone and arterial-stiffness measures
Null or negative findings: No demonstrated fracture, cardiovascular-event or lifespan reduction; renal-patient trials have mixed primary outcomes
Certainty: Moderate for vitamin K biomarkers; Low for surrogate bone/vascular benefits

Null or negative findings: No body-composition benefit in a 6 g/day trial; clinical-event prevention remains unproven
Certainty: Moderate for homocysteine; Low/insufficient for clinical outcomes

Studied doses and populations: Approximately 1–2 g/day; healthy older, overweight/obese and clinical populations
Null or negative findings: High-dose obesity trial did not improve insulin sensitivity; another trial increased muscle metabolites without improving mitochondrial or metabolic outcomes
Certainty: High for pharmacodynamic NAD effects; Low for functional benefits; insufficient for lifespan

Strongest human evidence: Q-SYMBIO in chronic heart failure; mixed symptom meta-analyses
Studied doses and populations: 300 mg/day for two years in heart failure; heterogeneous doses in statin trials
Supported findings: Q-SYMBIO reported fewer long-term major cardiovascular events in moderate-to-severe heart failure
Null or negative findings: Short-term Q-SYMBIO endpoints were negative; statin-myalgia meta-analysis found no benefit
Certainty: Moderate in adjunctive heart-failure treatment; Low/inconsistent for statin symptoms; not general longevity evidence

Supported findings: Studies report improvements in selected computerized cognitive domains
Null or negative findings: No independent large replication, dementia endpoint or functional outcome; substantial multiplicity concerns

Strongest human evidence: Twelve-month SmartAge RCT plus pharmacokinetic study
Studied doses and populations: 0.9 mg/day wheat-germ extract in SmartAge; higher-dose PK investigation
Supported findings: Exploratory verbal-memory or inflammation signals only
Null or negative findings: SmartAge was negative for its primary memory outcome and secondary outcomes; oral spermidine did not increase plasma spermidine in the PK study
Certainty: Low for cognition; insufficient for longevity

Studied doses and populations: Usually several hundred milligrams/day; apparent signals around at least 500 mg/day
Supported findings: Small pooled BP reductions of approximately 2–3 mmHg
Null or negative findings: Results vary by meta-analysis, endpoint and subgroup; no demonstrated event or longevity reduction
Certainty: Low–Moderate for small BP effects; insufficient for longevity

Strongest human evidence: Small metabolic, MCI and cognition RCTs
Supported findings: Selected imaging or metabolic surrogate changes in some studies
Null or negative findings: No memory improvement in the MCI trial; other human metabolic trials are negative or inconsistent

Strongest human evidence: Preclinical lifespan experiments, narrative human review and ABLE protocol
Studied doses and populations: ABLE: sustained-release Ca-AKG 1 g/day planned for six months
Supported findings: Animal and mechanistic findings justify clinical research
Null or negative findings: No convincing published human evidence of extended lifespan, reduced morbidity or clinically meaningful healthy-aging benefit
Certainty: Very low/insufficient for human aging or longevity
